course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
module: Platform architecture, infobases and development environments
title: Where 1C runs: the platform, application and your data
goal: Distinguish Nexus, the platform, a configuration, an infobase and the two modes, then prepare a separate place for your first program.

prerequisites.text: Using Windows windows and folders is enough. No programming, existing infobase or BSL knowledge is assumed. Preparation is included in this lesson.

sections.title: Familiar work worth simplifying
paragraphs: Imagine a small repair workshop. Each day an employee records customers, services and requests, totals work duration and finds open requests. Paper can do this, but actions repeat and records are easy to lose. An application helps retain information and apply agreed rules. A developer describes the rules; a user works through the resulting windows.

1C programming can automate those repeated actions. Its script describes a calculation or a response to an event, for example. Code does not run by itself: the platform executes it in a particular part of the application. We therefore start with a map of the environment rather than unexplained source text.

sections.title: Three things to distinguish
paragraphs: The 1C:Enterprise platform is installed software for developing and running business applications. A configuration describes a particular application: its catalogs, documents, windows and rules. An infobase contains that configuration and its application data. We call it a base for short; that does not mean any arbitrary folder.

A player, a work’s description and your collection make a useful limited comparison, but do not take it as a literal file model. The practical distinction is action: installing a platform is not editing a customer; adding an application field changes configuration; renaming one customer changes data. Identical configurations in separate infobases do not automatically synchronise their records.

sections.title: Two modes of one base, and Nexus
paragraphs: Designer is for changing configuration: a developer opens the object tree and modules there. Enterprise mode runs the application: a user sees lists and cards. These are different roles of one product. An empty application may have few commands; installing the platform does not create a ready-made service.

Nexus provides the lesson, reference and an optional browser draft. Saving a self-report here does not run 1C or save a customer card in the external infobase. Keep the lesson open beside the actual training application. Before acting, name the application: “I am reading Nexus” or “I am opening Designer”.

diagram.text:
Nexus: read and compare
1C → selected training infobase

    Enterprise: run and observe

sections.title: Create your separate learning space
paragraphs: If 1C is not installed, use the official training-version page below and follow the supplier’s download, licence and installation instructions. Nexus does not distribute the platform installer. If a suitable legally installed platform already runs, you need not reinstall it. Without the platform you can read the lesson, but the practical work remains not performed, rather than becoming successful through a note.

In the 1C launcher choose Add → Create a new infobase → Without configuration for development. Select a local location, a clear name such as NexusReferenceProgramming and a new separate empty folder. Before finishing, compare it with working infobase folders: it must be different. If the folder already contains a base, cancel and choose another new folder. The list name is a convenient label; the directory identifies the storage being opened.

Select the new item and open Designer. If no configuration tree is shown, choose Configuration → Open configuration. Then open the same infobase in Enterprise mode: an empty configuration has no customer or service lists yet. That is expected. Close the user window before the next edit. Never load a training configuration over existing data. The applied 1C course separately explains loading a ready-made service; the first message does not need it.

sections.title: Where the first program will live
paragraphs: A module stores code in a configuration. The platform calls suitable code in response to an event, such as application startup. You need not create catalogs or custom forms yet. In the next lesson we open this empty training base’s managed application module and display one message.

Predict the preparation result: the launcher has a separate item with your directory; Designer opens its configuration; Enterprise has no customers yet. If you see working data instead, stop and close that window: another infobase was selected. An empty new base is expected and is not a reason to reinstall.

sections.title: Check your orientation without code
paragraphs: Open your own item in both modes, one at a time. Record its chosen name and directory, what each mode showed, and which actions would change configuration versus data. Do not include real customer names or information from other infobases.
If the platform is unavailable, say so. Explaining the map is useful but does not replace actual preparation. Before the next lesson you need a real separate base and access to Designer.

practice.title: On your own: a separate base for first experiments
practice.task: Create a separate empty infobase named NexusReferenceProgramming and open it in Designer and Enterprise, one at a time. Check its directory first. Record actual observations and explain why no customers are expected.
practice.environment: Official installed 1C in a separate training infobase. Nexus shows the lesson and keeps an optional draft; it does not run this program.
practice.externalRoute: Follow the steps labelled by application. The self-report field records your external observation; it is not Nexus verification.

criteria: The directory differs from working infobases.
Unperformed actions are stated honestly; a note is not described as execution.
practice.hint: First compare the path in the launcher; similar window titles do not prove that the infobase is the same.

referenceSolution.source: The platform is installed separately from Nexus. I selected and checked a new empty folder for NexusReferenceProgramming. Designer shows the empty application description; Enterprise has no customers yet. Adding a field would change configuration; entering a customer would change data. Another base with the same configuration does not automatically share records. State your actual actions; say so if a mode was not opened.
paragraphs: A reference for reasoning and expected observation. It neither fills your record nor certifies completion.
